input.prompt: A professional woman seated at her desk in a bright modern office, listening. The camera is locked and stationary: ZERO zoom, push-in, pull-out, pan, tilt, crop, reframing, perspective shift or drift. The framing, camera position, subject scale, desk visibility and background composition at the LAST FRAME must be visually identical to the FIRST FRAME - the desk, mug and notebook stay fully in frame the whole clip. She is NOT speaking: lips closed throughout, no lip, mouth or jaw movement. Her eyes look directly into the camera lens the entire clip - no downward glance, side glance, gaze shift, eye wandering or half-lidded look. Only 1-2 brief blinks; eyes otherwise open and steady. A neutral attentive expression that never changes. Head, hair and facial motion at the minimum natural level - only faint breathing. No head turns, tilts, nodding, leaning or gestures. Hands stay as in the source image, loosely clasped and still on the desk. Preserve her face, hair, wardrobe, lighting, colour, the office and desk objects as shown; do not brighten, lift the shadows or re-grade. Wall logo and mug lettering unchanged.
input.negative_prompt: gaze shift, looking down, looking away, eye wandering, head tilt, expression change, excessive facial motion, camera movement, zoom, push-in, pull-out, pan, tilt, reframing, crop, camera drift, perspective shift, speaking, talking, mouth opening, lip movement, gesturing, hand movement, leaning, cut, transition, face change, lighting change, brightening, re-grading, added text, watermark, distortion, warping, morphing

correction.why: Kling lifted exposure 2.59% peak / 2.27% mean across the 5 s. Known Kling behaviour; the negative prompt does not prevent it.
correction.method: Per-frame per-channel linear gain returning each frame's RGB channel means to frame 0's. Frame 0 is the reference and carries NO gain. Measured gain range 0.97273 - 1.00000, all <= 1.0, so the correction only scales down - no highlight clipping is possible.
correction.swing_is_one_sided: 0 of 121 frames are darker than frame 0, so Diane's clamp-to-1.0 method applies cleanly here (unlike take 2, whose swing was two-sided).

fps_note: Base is 24 fps. LatentSync normalises output to 25 fps regardless of input, so the 16-frame padding must be computed at 25 fps (locked rule 3).
